climate.overview_html: The pre-COP31 diplomatic picture sharpened on 22 October as China published its formal Antalya priorities: a detailed roadmap for delivering the US$300 billion annual climate-finance goal, rejection of European carbon border adjustment mechanisms as disguised trade barriers, and a pledge to defend developing-nation interests on both mitigation and adaptation finance. The backdrop remains the UN Secretary-General’s 21 October declaration that the world is falling “dangerously short” on climate action. In a separate setback for COP31’s scientific underpinning, the IPCC’s plenary in Addis Ababa was suspended on 16 October without agreement on the AR7 timeline after Saudi Arabia, India and China pushed for a 2029 completion over the 2028 target needed to inform the second global stocktake; the session overran, forcing smaller delegations from least-developed countries and small island states to leave before a vote could be held. IPCC chair Jim Skea on 19 October called for a swift resolution, warning COP31’s loss-and-damage and adaptation tracks may proceed without an agreed scientific baseline.

items.headline: China Sets COP31 Antalya Priorities: Demands Detailed Roadmap for US$300 Billion Annual Climate Finance Goal, Opposes Carbon Border Mechanisms as Trade Barriers, Pledges to Speak for Developing Nations
items.summary: China's Vice Minister of Ecology and Environment Li Gao published Beijing's COP31 positions on October 21–22. Top priorities: (1) compelling developed countries to deliver a concrete implementation roadmap for the US$300 billion annual climate finance goal agreed at COP29, with transparent accounting; (2) opposing the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and similar unilateral trade-linked climate measures as violations of UNFCCC common-but-differentiated responsibilities; (3) demanding the global stocktake focus on the implementation gap in developed-nation commitments rather than on developing-nation ambitions; (4) tripling adaptation finance. Li Gao said China would attend at the highest level. The positions set up a significant clash with the EU and some of the Turkish presidency's electrification targets at Antalya. China separately noted it wants detailed talks on a roadmap for the developed-country $300B goal for 2035 and called for a positive trade and climate nexus rather than unilateral border measures.

items.headline: UN Secretary-General Guterres: World Falling “Dangerously Short” on Climate Action Ahead of COP31; El Niño and Record Heat Amplify Urgency
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres issued a stark statement on October 21 calling the world 'dangerously short' on climate action, referencing record-breaking heat, devastating floods, and an unprecedented El Niño as making accelerated action 'ever more urgent.' A concurrent UN news release ('As disasters mount, next UN climate summit faces a test of trust') emphasised that the NCQG agreed at COP29 must be operationalised, and that the UNFCCC process faces a credibility crisis with climate-vulnerable nations. The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 found that even full delivery of existing pledges leads to 2.6°C. With COP31 in Antalya opening November 9 and a World Leaders' Summit set for November 11–12, diplomatic pressure is intensifying.

items.source: The Standard HK / CTV News / Reuters / Al-Monitor
items.headline: IPCC Plenary Suspended in Addis Ababa Without Agreement on AR7 Timeline: Saudi Arabia, India and China Back 2029 Delay Over 2028 Target; Small-Island and LDC Delegations Walk Out as Session Overruns; IPCC Chair Skea Calls for Swift Resolution (19 Oct)
items.summary: The IPCC's plenary meeting in Addis Ababa, convened to agree on the Seventh Assessment Report (AR7) timeline, was suspended on October 16 without agreement after running past its scheduled close. Saudi Arabia, India and China argued for delaying final AR7 publication to 2029, citing the need to incorporate more science from developing nations; the EU and AOSIS bloc want the report by 2028 to inform the second global stocktake. Because the meeting overran, delegations from least-developed countries and small island developing states were forced to leave before a vote, which IPCC chair Jim Skea flagged on October 19 as a structural fairness problem that 'disproportionately disadvantaged' the most climate-vulnerable nations. Skea said discussions 'remain open' and the IPCC will reconvene at the earliest opportunity. Notably, the Addis Ababa meeting did reach consensus on guidelines for artificial intelligence use within IPCC assessments — the one productive outcome of the session. The AR7 impasse risks leaving COP31 loss-and-damage and adaptation finance tracks without a mutually agreed scientific baseline.

items.headline: South Africa at COP31: As Climate Shocks Intensify, Pretoria Pushes for Substantially More Adaptation Finance; Aligns with G77 Demand to Triple Adaptation Funding by 2035
items.summary: South Africa is entering COP31 with adaptation finance as its top priority, arguing that developing nations most vulnerable to climate shocks have been shortchanged in NCQG negotiations dominated by mitigation framing. The Daily Maverick piece cites intensifying floods, drought cycles, and coastal erosion in southern Africa as the political driver. South Africa aligns with G77 demands for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, mirroring the European Parliament's October resolution position. The piece notes that while adaptation funding pledges have grown, actual disbursements remain far below commitments — a structural issue South Africa and the African Group plan to press at Antalya.

major_events.name: Typhoon Champi (Rosal) — LAND WARNING Issued for Taiwan 22 Oct; Storm ~520 km ESE, Winds 184 kph Gusts 227 kph; China (Zhejiang/Fujian) Begins Coastal Evacuations; Landfall Near Eastern Taiwan Expected Fri–Sat
major_events.status: As of 22 Oct 11:00 local: Taiwan’s CWA issued a land warning for Typhoon Champi covering Yilan, Hualien, Taitung and Pingtung counties. The storm is approximately 520 km east-southeast of Oluanpi (Taiwan’s southernmost point), moving northwest at 15–20 kph with maximum sustained winds of 184 kph (gusts to 227 kph) and a 320 km wind radius. JTWC maintains low track-confidence throughout; the China National Meteorological Centre expects eastern Taiwan landfall around Saturday as a strong typhoon. China’s coastal provinces of Zhejiang and Fujian have activated typhoon emergency responses and begun evacuating vulnerable coastal residents. Airports in Shanghai, Hangzhou, Ningbo, Fuzhou and Wenzhou are on disruption watch. Taiwan’s Central Mountain Range may stall the storm’s translation speed, extending the heavy-rain window. The US–Japan Keen Sword military exercise was disrupted by the approach.
major_events.impact: Taiwan: land warning active (Yilan, Hualien, Taitung, Pingtung); 125+ domestic flights cancelled 22 Oct; heavy to torrential rain east coast and spreading north/central Taiwan Thu–Sat; mainland China: Zhejiang and Fujian coastal evacuations under way, Shanghai/Hangzhou/Fuzhou airports on disruption watch; Japan Ryukyu Islands: possible late-week effects; Keen Sword US–Japan exercise disrupted; Guam: post-passage damage assessment ongoing

major_events.name: SE Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia/Borneo/Sumatra) — Day 25+ — ASMC Level 3 Alert Ongoing; 283,270+ Respiratory Cases; Smoke Now Reaching Papua New Guinea Capital
major_events.status: As of 22 Oct: No significant change since 21 Oct. Indonesia’s health ministry recorded 283,270 respiratory illness cases across seven provinces as of 13 October (likely higher now). More than 69,000 firefighters remain deployed; 223 individuals and 9 companies face legal action. Transboundary smoke has reached Papua New Guinea’s capital Port Moresby and India’s Great Nicobar Island. Super El Niño and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole continue to suppress rainfall across fire-prone Borneo and Sumatra. ASEAN pre-summit enforcement review is scheduled for November.
major_events.impact: Four confirmed deaths; hundreds of thousands receiving respiratory treatment across seven Indonesian provinces and neighbouring countries; schools closed in parts of Malaysia and East Timor; Singapore legal actions against 7 companies ongoing; haze reaching PNG and Indian Ocean territories

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Champi escalated sharply overnight from a potential sea-warning scenario to an active land warning. Taiwan’s CWA issued the land warning on 22 October covering Yilan, Hualien, Taitung and Pingtung, as the storm — now ~520 km ESE with 184 kph winds and 227 kph gusts and a 320 km radius — tracks northwest toward an expected Friday–Saturday close approach or landfall. China has begun coastal evacuations in Zhejiang and Fujian; over 125 Taiwan domestic flights were cancelled. Focus Taiwan confirms JTWC carries low track-confidence throughout, meaning the landfall position remains uncertain. The SE Asian transboundary haze continues into Day 25+ with no change from yesterday’s status.

items.source: Taipei Times / Focus Taiwan / CWA Taiwan / The Standard HK / SCMP
items.headline: Taiwan Issues Land Warning for Typhoon Champi: Storm ~520 km ESE, Winds 184 kph Gusts 227 kph; Closest Approach Fri–Sat; China (Zhejiang/Fujian) Begins Coastal Evacuations; 125+ Taiwan Flights Cancelled; Terrain-Stall Risk Flagged
items.summary: On October 22, Taiwan's Central Weather Administration issued a land warning covering Yilan, Hualien, Taitung and Pingtung counties. As of 11am local time the storm was ~520 km east-southeast of Oluanpi, moving northwest at 15–20 kph, with maximum sustained winds of 184 kph and gusts to 227 kph — a 320 km wind radius covering most of the island. JTWC's official track carries low confidence throughout. China's National Meteorological Centre projects an eastern Taiwan landfall around Saturday as a strong typhoon. Taiwan's transport ministry reported 125+ domestic flight cancellations. President Lai Ching-te urged preparedness and avoidance of mountains and coasts. China's Zhejiang and Fujian provinces activated their highest-tier typhoon responses and began evacuating coastal residents, with airport disruption watches for Shanghai, Hangzhou, Ningbo, Fuzhou and Wenzhou. Meteorologists flagged that Taiwan's Central Mountain Range could stall the storm, extending the heavy-rain window. The US–Japan Keen Sword military exercise was disrupted. The SCMP described Champi as the strongest storm of 2026, having earlier reached Category 5 equivalent over the Philippine Sea.

items.source: Al Jazeera / France 24 / Indonesia Ministry of Health / Wikipedia
items.headline: SE Asian Haze Day 25+: 283,270 Respiratory Cases in Indonesia as of 13 Oct; Smoke Reaches Papua New Guinea Capital Port Moresby; 69,000+ Firefighters Deployed; Al Jazeera: “Crisis Will Persist Until Polluters Pay”
items.summary: The Southeast Asian transboundary haze emergency continues into its 25th day-plus with no significant status change since October 21. Indonesia's health ministry recorded 283,270 respiratory illness cases across seven provinces as of October 13 — actual figures are higher. Over 637,000 hectares burned January–August 2026, per environmental group Auriga. Indonesia has deployed more than 69,000 firefighting personnel; 223 individuals and nine companies face legal action. Transboundary smoke has now reached Papua New Guinea's capital Port Moresby and India's Great Nicobar Island. An Al Jazeera opinion piece (October 20) argues the crisis 'will persist until polluters pay,' citing failures of corporate accountability under ASEAN's transboundary haze framework. The super El Niño and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole continue to suppress monsoon rainfall over Borneo and Sumatra.

renewables.overview_html: Storage headline of the week: AMEA Power signed agreements on 16 October for a 250 MW/1,000 MWh battery project in Uzbekistan’s Bukhara region — the largest standalone battery storage commitment in Central Asia this year — adding to the UAE-backed developer’s existing 150 MW/300 MWh Tashkent system (under construction since May 2026) and bringing its total committed Uzbekistan storage to 400 MW/1,300 MWh. Meanwhile, EirGrid’s data showing 15% of Ireland’s wind wasted in H1 2026 continues to resonate as a cautionary data point for Europe’s grid-investment gap, while institutional capital flows into operational storage: Foresight completed its acquisition of Finland’s Nivala BESS this week.

items.headline: AMEA Power Signs Agreements for 250 MW/1,000 MWh Battery Storage Project in Uzbekistan’s Bukhara Region; Central Asia’s Largest Battery Commitment This Year; Executed at Tashkent Energy Sector Investors’ Council 16 Oct
items.summary: UAE-based AMEA Power signed project agreements on October 16 for a 250 MW / 1,000 MWh battery energy storage system in Uzbekistan's Bukhara region (Gijduvan district), announced publicly October 20. The deal was executed at the Energy Sector Investors' Council meeting in Tashkent. It follows AMEA Power's existing 150 MW / 300 MWh BESS under construction near Tashkent (ground broken May 2026, estimated at ~US$86 million with EBRD financing under consideration). Combined, AMEA Power's total committed Uzbekistan storage is 400 MW / 1,300 MWh. Uzbekistan has been aggressively contracting battery storage to complement growing wind and solar capacity and stabilise a grid suffering from intermittency. AMEA Power, backed by Abdul Latif Jameel, operates renewable and storage projects in 35 countries. No deal price for the Bukhara project was disclosed.

items.headline: EirGrid Data: 15% of Ireland’s Wind Electricity Wasted H1 2026 Due to Grid Constraints; Enough to Power 667,000 Homes; 13%+ of All Renewables Curtailed in First Nine Months; Grid Investment Lag Worsening
items.summary: New EirGrid figures published by RTÉ on October 21 reveal that more than 13% of available wind and solar electricity in Ireland during the first nine months of 2026 could not be used. Wind Energy Ireland's analysis focused on the H1 figure: 15% of wind electricity was dispatched down in H1 2026 — enough to power approximately 667,000 Irish homes. The figures represent a worsening from 2025 curtailment rates and are above EirGrid's ECP-2.3 projections. Experts cite a multi-year lag between accelerating renewable capacity additions and major transmission infrastructure investment, with Grid West and the North-South interconnector still years from completion. The pattern mirrors wider European grid constraint issues highlighted in recent Ember and ENTSO-E analyses.

items.headline: XCF Global Completes All-Stock Three-Way Merger Combining Renewable Fuel Production, Biomass-to-Fuels Development (Southern Energy Renewables) and Carbon-Asset Monetisation (DevvStream); Creates Integrated Renewable Fuels Platform
items.summary: US-based XCF Global completed an all-stock three-way business combination on October 19, uniting: XCF's existing renewable fuel production and refining operations; Southern Energy Renewables' biomass-to-fuels development project pipeline; and DevvStream's environmental asset management and carbon credit monetisation platform. The merged entity targets the full lifecycle of biomass-based renewable fuel projects from production through carbon credit generation and sale. No financial terms or combined capacity figures were disclosed.

items.headline: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II Completes Acquisition of Nivala BESS — Finland’s Largest Battery Energy Storage System — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures; Nordic Grid-Balancing Assets Draw Continued Institutional Capital
items.summary: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II completed its acquisition of 100% of Nivala BESS — Finland's largest battery energy storage system — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures (FRV), the renewables subsidiary of Abdul Latif Jameel. No deal price was disclosed. Nivala provides frequency and voltage grid balancing services in Finland's electricity market, where curtailment pressure from growing intermittent renewable capacity is rising. The transaction continues a trend of institutional infrastructure funds acquiring operational Nordic BESS assets as ancillary services revenue models mature.

science.overview_html: The in-window research highlight is arXiv:2610.26145 (Addison, Kendon, Watson; 20 October), a NeurIPS 2026 climate-ML workshop paper tackling hourly precipitation downscaling from kilometre-scale regional climate simulations. Just outside the 7-day window but still the week’s dominant reference for ML weather practitioners: Mouatadid et al. in Nature (14 October) showed probabilistic bias correction doubles AI subseasonal forecast skill at 2–6 weeks and leads the SubX international competition, improving ECMWF’s dynamical model for 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. At the science-governance intersection, the IPCC plenary in Addis Ababa (16 October) reached consensus on guidelines for AI use within IPCC assessments — a notable policy milestone for ML applied to climate science, even as the broader AR7 timeline deadlocked.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.26145 — Hourly Precipitation Downscaling from km-Scale Regional Climate Simulations (Addison, Kendon, Watson); Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning
items.meta: Addison, Kendon, Watson · arXiv:2610.26145 [physics.ao-ph] · 20 Oct 2026 · NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning
items.summary: Henry Addison, Elizabeth Kendon and Peter Watson present a deep-learning approach to downscaling hourly precipitation from kilometre-scale regional climate model (RCM) simulations. As convection-permitting km-scale RCMs become computationally feasible for multi-decade runs, translating their output to finer scales relevant to impact applications (urban flooding, hydrology, agriculture) is a key bottleneck. The paper applies an ML downscaling method trained on km-scale RCM output to achieve improved hourly precipitation representation at sub-kilometre scales. Accepted to the Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning at NeurIPS 2026 — a primary venue for climate-AI research, where accepted work is now appearing on arXiv ahead of the December 2026 conference in Sydney. The work connects to the broader question of whether statistical downscaling can substitute for dynamical downscaling at the finest spatial scales relevant to adaptation planning.

items.headline: IPCC Reaches Consensus on Artificial Intelligence Guidelines for Climate Assessment at Addis Ababa Plenary; First Major IPCC Policy Decision on AI Use in Scientific Reports Amid Wider AR7 Timeline Deadlock
items.summary: Amid the broader failure to agree on the AR7 timeline, IPCC chair Jim Skea confirmed on October 19 that the Addis Ababa plenary did reach agreement on one substantive matter: guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence within IPCC scientific assessments. This marks the first time the IPCC has established formal policy on how AI-generated analysis, AI-assisted literature synthesis, or ML-based projections may be incorporated into its reports — a significant governance step given the rapid growth of ML in climate and atmospheric science. Details of the specific guidelines were not publicly released, but the agreement addresses concerns about AI reliability, reproducibility, and uncertainty quantification in a scientific assessment context. The broader AR7 timeline dispute remains unresolved, with the IPCC committed to reconvening 'at the earliest opportunity.'

items.title: XCF Global Completes All-Stock Three-Way Merger Combining Renewable Fuel Production, Biomass-to-Fuels Development (Southern Energy Renewables) and Environmental Asset Monetisation (DevvStream); Integrated Lifecycle Platform for Biomass-Based Fuels and Carbon Credits

The structure is designed to capture value under both low-carbon-intensity fuel standards and carbon credit frameworks in North America and Europe.
